blocks.text: Condo buildings in City of Mission
Briskham Manor — 7554 Briskham Street

Confirmed apartment-form. 33 units, Strata Plan LMS1049; frame wood with brick exterior and vinyl siding, 3 storeys. A well-managed 55+ complex; the sheet's bylaw fields record cats OK, dogs OK, a two-pet limit with restrictions, and listings describe pets limited to roughly 24–25 lbs. Gas and hot water are included in the strata fees per listings.
Mission Manor — 33165 2nd Avenue
Built 1992. The directory records restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed. Listings record frame-wood construction with stucco and underground parking.
Glenkirk Court — 7436 Stave Lake Street
Built 1975, 38 units. Listings note shared laundry, and one current listing states "No short term rentals" for the building.
Montgomery Condos — developer address 7375 Horne Street

(resale listings also address units at 33281 2 Avenue). Six storeys, 85 units, by Redekop Faye, with estimated completion in 2026 (developer source) — a presale/just-completed building, so REDMA applied to developer contracts. Current listings describe fall 2026 move-ins and note prices exclude GST — a new-build marker; verify the specific unit's status before relying on it.
Preston on Fourteenth ("The Preston") — 32690 14th Avenue

Built 2023 per current listings, by Redekop Faye. The presale record describes a 4-storey woodframe building of 103 condominiums plus 11 affordable rental units, and states condo rentals were permitted for 100 years under the project's housing agreement (presale source).
Ridgewood Place — 7265 Haig Street
Named in one current listing.
Stave Lake Landing — 33599 2nd Avenue

Built 1997. The directory records restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals not allowed — the rental line is void since November 24, 2022. The building's form (apartment vs townhome-style strata) was not fully settled from the directory snippet.

items.t: The page has no FAQ and no OCP-vs-zoning explainer; its five plan tiles are its whole substance.

On MLS®: "Mission" for market context means the Fraser Valley board community Mission, with nine sub-areas — Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission, Mission West, Stave Falls and Steelhead.
The rural sub-areas are detached-led shelves with little or no attached stock: five of the seven carry no attached listings at all.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the downtown/central core — 1st and 2nd Avenues, Horne Street, 7th Avenue and 14th Avenue (Montgomery, Mission Manor, Stave Lake Landing, Preston), the Cedar Street corridor in Cedar Valley (Silver & Cedar), and the Briskham Street pocket west of downtown (Briskham Manor, Briskham Hill).

The Silverdale planning geography: the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA) sits within the City's urban growth boundary and covers 1,392 ha (3,440 ac), bordered by Silverdale Creek to the east, rural, agricultural and Kwantlen First Nations lands to the north, Silvermere Lake to the west and the Fraser River and Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) lands to the south.

items.t: City plans: the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing and repealing Bylaw 6350-2025 and keeping the same vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction, with a Regional Context Statement formally incorporated as required under the Local Government Act. Zoning is Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020.

Silverdale layering: under the City's SCPA Neighbourhood Planning Terms of Reference (Policy LAN.64(C), adopted February 18, 2020), neighbourhood plans are required for SCPA areas anticipating growth in density or experiencing development pressures, and must be consistent with the OCP including its Development Permit Areas.

blocks.text: Good to know about City of Mission condos

items.t: Mission replaced its OCP in 2026, and the replacement changed almost nothing on purpose. Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replaced and repealed Bylaw 6350-2025 for a procedural reason (formally incorporating a Regional Context Statement), with the vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction unchanged. Planning documents that cite the old bylaw number are a bylaw out of date.

One developer is reshaping the city's condo map. Redekop Faye built Preston on Fourteenth (2023), Montgomery (completing 2026) and Silver & Cedar (completing 2026) — three of the city's newest apartment buildings share one builder, which makes cross-building comparisons of construction and warranty unusually direct.

Preston's rentals rest on a housing agreement, not just the 2022 law. Its presale record states condo rentals were permitted for 100 years — a project-level housing agreement term that survives independently of the province-wide voiding of rental bylaws.

Two Mission complexes each carry two addresses. Montgomery is marketed at 7375 Horne Street while resale listings address units at 33281 2 Avenue; Luther Place is 7525 Martin Place in listings and 32286 7th Avenue in the building directory. Confirm which address a specific unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents.

The DPA guidelines behind every plan area are mid-revision. The City is updating the OCP's Development Permit Area Guidelines, with a public hearing notice issued for August 17, 2026 — a parcel's permit-area obligations in Cedar Valley, Silverdale or Stave Heights may read differently once that review lands.

items.t: OCP frame — the City's own notice: the City of Mission's Notice of Public Hearing for Tuesday, April 7, 2026 (6:00 pm, City Hall, 8645 Stave Lake Street, Mission) names "OFFICIAL COMMUNITY PLAN BYLAW 6405-2026" and states its purpose is "to replace and repeal the Official Community Plan Bylaw 6350-2025," that the new bylaw is substantively the same Official Community Plan with the overall vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction unchanged, and that it is proposed to address a procedural matter related to the adoption of the 2025 OCP Bylaw and to formally incorporate a Regional Context Statement as required under the Local Government Act.

Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA): within the City's urban growth boundary, 1,392 ha (3,440 ac), bordered by Silverdale Creek to the east, rural, agricultural and Kwantlen First Nations lands to the north, Silvermere Lake to the west and the Fraser River and Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) lands to the south; under the City's SCPA Neighbourhood Planning Terms of Reference (Policy LAN.64(C), adopted February 18, 2020), neighbourhood plans are required for areas in the SCPA anticipating growth in density or experiencing development pressures, and must be consistent with the OCP including its Development Permit Areas.

Silverdale planning layering: significant portions of the Silverdale Master Infrastructure Strategy (MIS) — the 2018 technical strategy — have been superseded by the Central Neighbourhood Plan (CNP) and its supporting technical documents and by the Utilities Master Plan.

Development Permit Areas: the City is updating the existing Development Permit Area (DPA) Guidelines in Mission's Official Community Plan, with a further public hearing notice issued for August 17, 2026 pointing to the DPA Guidelines Review project page.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Mission

items.t: Development Permit Areas: DPA guidelines sit in the OCP and are under review (public hearing notice Aug 17, 2026) — a hillside (Stave Heights) or environmentally sensitive lot's buildable area can be set by its DPA, so confirm overlays per parcel with the City.

Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha).

City of Mission property taxes — CITY regime only: 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, and a flat 10% penalty is added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026; the City states it has no authority to waive or modify the penalty amounts (Community Charter ss. 233–234 frame). The City does not accept credit card payments.

Rural regime — kept strictly separate, not the City rule: FVRD electoral areas outside the City follow the rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11: 5% after Jul 2 + 5% after Oct 31). That regime does not apply inside the City of Mission — do not blend the two.
Supreme Court registry: Mission has no Supreme Court registry.

faq.q: What is the City of Mission's current OCP bylaw, and when was it adopted?
faq.a: Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replaces Bylaw 6350-2025. The vision, land use framework, mapping and policy direction are unchanged, and a Regional Context Statement is formally incorporated.

faq.q: Is Cherry Lane a condo or a townhouse complex?
faq.a: Townhouse strata. The building directory's own product variants for Cherry Lane (32165 Seventh Avenue, built 1989, 22 units) include "Townhouse," and the same is true of Luther Place (36 units, Strata Plan NWS2729), whose MLS records state dwelling type Townhouse outright.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Mission condo?
faq.a: For a long-term tenancy, yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, which is why the "rentals not allowed" directory lines for Cherry Lane and Stave Lake Landing are outdated law. Short-term rentals are different: a bylaw can still restrict them, and one current Glenkirk Court listing states "No short term rentals."

faq.q: Do the new Redekop Faye buildings charge GST?
faq.a: Yes on developer sales — Montgomery and Silver & Cedar are new construction, so 5% GST applies, with the First-Time Home Buyers' GST rebate (up to $50,000 back on homes to $1 million) and the BC Newly Built Home Exemption (PTT fully exempt to $1.1 million) both in play for qualifying buyers. Preston (built 2023) is now resale stock, so a purchase there is generally GST-exempt.

faq.q: How big is Silverdale, and can I buy a lot there today?
faq.a: The Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area is 1,392 ha (3,440 ac) inside the urban growth boundary, governed by the neighbourhood-plan process (Policy LAN.64(C), adopted February 18, 2020).

faq.q: Do I own the land in a Mission park?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA.

faq.q: Which OCP bylaw governs a Mission parcel, and when was it adopted?
faq.a: Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted June 1, 2026, replacing Bylaw 6350-2025 with the framework unchanged plus a formal Regional Context Statement. Confirm which number the City currently cites before putting one in an offer.

faq.q: How does Mission's tax penalty work if my completion straddles early July?
faq.a: Hard date: Taxes were due July 2, 2026 and the flat 10% penalty lands July 3, 2026 on outstanding current balances including unclaimed home owner grants, with no City discretion to waive it. That is the city regime — not the rural 5% + 5% regime, which is a different regime for FVRD electoral areas.

faq.q: Two Mission complexes carry two addresses — does that matter?
faq.a: Confirm which address a specific unit's title and strata records use before ordering documents. Neither complex is duplex stock.

faq.a: 1,392 ha (3,440 ac) inside the City's urban growth boundary, bordered by Silverdale Creek to the east, Silvermere Lake to the west and the Fraser River and ALR lands to the south, per the City's SCPA Neighbourhood Planning Terms of Reference (Policy LAN.64(C), adopted February 18, 2020).
